This public-safe study note summarizes general pump reliability concepts. It is not a maintenance procedure. Common early indicators of pump problems can include rising vibration, unusual noise, seal leakage, bearing temperature increases, flow instability, suction pressure changes, discharge pressure changes, and motor current changes. These indicators are more useful when viewed as trends rather than isolated points. Reliability analysis often combines operator rounds, historian trends, maintenance history, process context, and inspection findings. A single data point is rarely enough to identify root cause. For example, vibration can be related to cavitation, misalignment, bearing wear, process conditions, or instrumentation problems. Good analytics tools should help prioritize attention and show evidence. They should not hide uncertainty.
